title: Temporal Mosaic Allocator: staggered-slot anchoring to minimize KV fragmentation under continuous batching
creator: Aisha Varma
description: Introduce a new allocation strategy (Temporal Mosaic Allocator) that reduces KV cache fragmentation by anchoring hot token slots in staggered time windows and performing low-latency background relocations aligned to batch boundaries. Target is to reduce usable free-run fragmentation by 40% and p99 generation latency regressions from defrag by 50% compared to current baseline.
background: Current continuous-batching workload causes frequent small evictions and many tiny holes in GPU-resident KV slabs. Existing slab allocators maintain high throughput but lead to fragmentation that increases effective memory pressure, forcing model downsizing or extra reserved capacity. Previous tickets tackled compaction passes and soft reserves, but we still observe: (1) oscillating free-run length distribution correlated with batch arrival jitter, (2) costly synchronous compaction during hot-path allocations, (3) poor locality for prefix reuse across concurrent requests.
proposal: Design a Temporal Mosaic Allocator with three core concepts: (1) staggered-slot anchoring: divide GPU KV space into time-anchored micro-arenas where allocations are preferentially placed based on token lifetime prediction; (2) eviction weave: an opportunistic, batch-aligned relocation that migrates small fragments into contiguous segments using the same GPU stream as generation to hide copy cost; (3) adaptive microcompaction: lightweight, incremental compaction triggered by fragmentation heuristics (fragmentation density and batch-alignment score) rather than absolute occupancy. The allocator integrates with continuous batching by attaching per-batch hints to allocations (expected prefix snapshots, TTL buckets).
detailed_design: Allocator layout: split KV memory into N micro-arenas (~4-16MB each) mapped to CUDA memory streams. Each arena has a primary island for short-lived tokens and a secondary island for longer-lived tokens; allocation policy uses a TTL histogram to map token to island. Anchoring: when a token is placed, record an anchor epoch equal to allocation_batch_id % anchor_stride; this staggers reclamation points across arenas. Eviction weave: during batch flush we perform small, in-place remap operations for entries with anchor_epoch equal to current epoch +/- window, grouping scattered entries into a destination slab using coalescing writes (vectorized memcopies). Relocation worker: runs on a low-priority CPU/GPU stream and performs two-phase handoff (reserve destination region, write new KV, atomically swap pointer) to avoid long pauses. Soft-fallback: if relocation would exceed per-request latency budget, cancel and mark token as anchored for next epoch. Microcompaction heuristic: fragmentation_score = weighted_sum(gap_count_density, avg_gap_size, batch_misalignment_ratio). We trigger microcompaction when fragmentation_score > threshold and available background bandwidth > min_bandwidth. Integration with continuous batching: batch metadata carries 'reuse_likelihood' and 'expected_length' to guide placement; the runtime marks hot prefixes to keep in primary islands. Memory accounting: arenas expose free-run histograms and high-water marks; allocator attempts to keep high-water marks below 85% in steady state by gradually expanding anchors and increasing background compaction frequency.
telemetry_and_metrics: free_run_distribution: histogram of contiguous free range sizes per-GPU
microcompaction_time_per_mb: median and p95 background compaction throughput
eviction_weave_pause_ms: distribution of any blocking pause introduced by in-band relocations
memory_headroom: percent free bytes usable without triggering large compaction
reuse_hit_rate: percent of allocations that hit anchored primary island for the same prefix within TTL
rollout_plan: 1) Implement allocator behind feature flag and unit tests in runtime branch (ENG-642420-fg)
2) Run synthetic microbenchmarks: tail-heavy chat, short-turn multi-user, long-context streaming. Compare fragmentation metrics to baseline.
3) Canary to small dedicated cluster with non-critical tenants and 24/7 observability (2 days), enable telemetry dashboards.
4) Monitor for regression signals for 72h; rollback if eviction_weave_pause_ms > 5ms p99 or p99_generation_latency regresses > 10%.
5) Gradual ramp to 20%, 50%, 100% and enable adaptive thresholds tuning based on observed reuse_hit_rate.
6) Post-rollout: bake for 2 weeks, then remove feature flag after stability confirmation.
tasks: Allocator prototype in C++ with mock GPU streams (Jonah)
Unit and integration tests including race and atomic-swap correctness (SRE pair)
Benchmark harness: synthetic workloads + replay traces from production (Bench team)
Canary rollout orchestration and rollback automation (Infra)
Performance tuning: anchor_stride, arena sizes, microcompaction thresholds (Engineers)
Documentation: design doc, operator runbook, feature flag docs (PM)
risks: Relocation write amplification: extra copies could increase GPU memory bandwidth usage and impact throughput
Atomic swap races with concurrent readers if pointer exchange ordering not handled correctly
Heuristic miscalibration: aggressive compaction could worsen tail latency under bursty traffic
Complexity of multi-stream coordination on heterogeneous GPUs may expose device-specific bugs
notes: Related research: 'Epochal slot anchoring for low-latency allocation' (internal whitepaper)
